answer: According to Section 40 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the right of private defence of the body commences as soon as there is a reasonable apprehension of danger from an attempt or threat to commit an offence, and it continues as long as that apprehension persists (chunk__section__BNS_S40, Section 40). Similarly, the right of private defence of property begins when there is a reasonable apprehension of danger to the property and continues under specific conditions, such as until the offender has retreated or the property has been recovered (chunk__section__BNS_S43, Section 43).
summary_answer: The right of private defence starts when there is a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body or property and continues as long as that apprehension exists.
detailed_answer: According to Section 40 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, the right of private defence of the body commences as soon as there is a reasonable apprehension of danger from an attempt or threat to commit an offence, and it continues as long as that apprehension persists (chunk__section__BNS_S40, Section 40). Similarly, the right of private defence of property begins when there is a reasonable apprehension of danger to the property and continues under specific conditions, such as until the offender has retreated or the property has been recovered (chunk__section__BNS_S43, Section 43).
final_answer: The right of private defence starts with a reasonable apprehension of danger and ends when that apprehension ceases.
